chapters.title: Intro: the ERP date isn't a factory promise
Machine state, tooling, labor and material release
When the five-axis machine fails and constraints collide
ERP, MES, the scheduling layer and Microsoft architecture

takeaways: An ERP date states intent; a finite, constraint-based schedule tests every operation against real resources, tooling, skills, material release and time windows.
Hard constraints decide feasibility first, while soft constraints and visible priority policies decide which feasible schedule the plant prefers.
ERP, MES and the scheduling layer each keep their own job, with Microsoft Fabric and Power BI providing governed history and visibility rather than acting as the scheduling engine.
hook: Production plans that look fine in ERP fall apart when a machine fails, a fixture is busy or material is still in inspection. This episode walks manufacturing planners, IT/OT architects and operations leaders through constraint-based scheduling in a hypothetical machining plant, showing how to turn factory facts into rules a scheduling engine can test and produce schedules people can actually run.
